_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY — placeholders. Copy to secrets.<env>.json (git-ignored), fill real values there. Never commit real secrets. See README.md → 'Environments' and 'Secrets to replace for production'.
_comment_environment: 'environment' is LOAD-BEARING: it yields the env code (development->dev, production->prod) that prefixes every project-global GCP id and names the per-environment state bucket. Teardown destroys the WORKLOAD layer only for EVERY environment (the DNS zone + state bucket are always preserved — they cost almost nothing to keep); a non-production 'teardown --purge' ALSO destroys the DNS zone + state bucket + sweeps secrets (production forbids --purge). Run 'spacestroker-deploy validate' to see every derived id.
_comment_monitoring: MONITORING (production only): the dashboard, uptime checks and Cloud Armor log-based metrics are created whenever 'environment' is production -- there is no toggle to set, the deploy tool derives it. The BUDGET additionally needs billingAccountId + alertEmail; leave either empty and the budget and its notification channel are simply SKIPPED (the apply still succeeds). A budget is created against the BILLING ACCOUNT, which sits ABOVE the project, so the deploying principal also needs roles/billing.costsManager granted THERE -- no project-level role provides it. Both fields are plain config rather than credentials, but never commit real values. Enable the two APIs first: gcloud services enable monitoring.googleapis.com billingbudgets.googleapis.com
_comment_orbit: ORBIT (#121/#122/#123) — three secrets, and PRODUCTION MUST SET ALL THREE. The custody keypair is SEPARATE from the payout keypair on purpose: sharing them makes 'player balances vs on-chain balance' uncheckable and turns an Orbit stake into a same-account no-op transfer. ⚠️ Committed config ships a REAL devnet Orbit keypair so the local stack works out of the box, so an environment that omits PublicKey/PrivateKey boots with Orbit ENABLED against devnet instead of failing closed — override both explicitly. The session secret signs the ~7-day read tokens; rotating it signs everyone out (contained: one signature recovers). The Telegram bot token sits in the PATH of every Bot API call, which is why the whole URL is treated as a secret and never logged; leave it OUT (or blank) and Telegram is simply INERT — no calls, and the modal hides the section.
_comment_clusterUrl: GeneralSettings:Token:ClusterUrl is a SECRET, not appConfig: the RPC provider's api-key rides in the URL's query string, and appConfig entries become plaintext Cloud Run env vars. Devnet form: https://devnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=... The FALLBACK below is a plain public endpoint with no key, so it stays in appConfig.
_comment_houseSeed: House seed bet (#168), PRODUCTION-ONLY: the house wallet places one ordinary paid stake into every newly opened round, so a round is never empty and a single real player can start it. BOTH halves are required and a MOCK_ value counts as ABSENT (HouseSeedSettings.IsConfigured is fail-CLOSED), so a half-filled block silently disables seeding instead of erroring — and the 'not configured' line logs at Information, which Production's Warning floor drops. It MUST be a separate keypair from TokenOwner* (identical sender and recipient makes the SPL transfer a 0-delta no-op that is then refused as underpaid, AFTER it confirms) and from Orbit (that is player CUSTODY money).
_comment_referralPayout: REFERRAL PAYOUT (#177), the dedicated account partners are paid FROM — the fourth keypair in the system, and deliberately NOT the treasury, the Orbit custody account or the house seed (the resolver REFUSES to configure on collision with any of them, so a referral-maths bug can drain at most the referral float). BOTH halves are required and a MOCK_ value counts as ABSENT (ReferralPayoutSettings.IsConfigured is fail-CLOSED), so a half-filled block silently disables cash-out instead of erroring: the partner page still renders earnings, the button just never works, and the 'not configured' line logs at Information, which Production's Warning floor drops. ⚠️ THE PUBLIC HALF LIVES IN appConfig AND THE PRIVATE HALF IN secrets — they are in different blocks, which is exactly how the public one got forgotten when this shipped. The account must also be FUNDED: a configured-but-empty account passes IsConfigured and then fails the solvency guard on every cash-out, reversing each one. ⚠️ PARTNERS THEMSELVES ARE NO LONGER CONFIG — they are rows in the ReferralPartners table (GeneralSettings:Operator:DefaultPartners is only a create-only startup seed), so a fresh environment has NO partners until someone inserts one by hand. ⚠️ The alert for a dry referral account is gated on gcp.alertEmail: leave it empty and the policy is SKIPPED, the apply still succeeds, and nobody is told.
_comment_hyperRoll: HYPER ROLL (#183), player-vs-house. It adds NO new secret: bets go into, and winners are paid from, the EXISTING treasury (TokenOwnerPublicKey in appConfig / TokenOwnerPrivateKey in secrets). ⚠️ FUND THE TREASURY BEFORE THE FIRST ROUND OPENS: every win is paid from the treasury's own balance, not from the round's stakes, and a win the balance cannot cover is NOT paid — the bet goes to NeedsManualAnalysis for a human. Size the treasury with the max stake: 0.1 SOL was chosen against a 20 SOL treasury (on the launch board, a 0.41% chance of an unpaid win over 1,000 worst-case max bets and 1.97% over 10,000 — specs/hyper-roll.md decisions 30 and 37); rule of thumb, max stake ≈ treasury ÷ 200. The same treasury also pays Cosmic Sprint. GeneralSettings:Operator:DefaultGames:1:HouseEdge:MaximumStake overrides the launch max stake baked into spacestrokersettings.json (0.1). ⚠️ TWO TRAPS. (1) IT IS INDEX-BASED: DefaultGames:1 is Hyper Roll only while spacestrokersettings.json lists Cosmic Sprint, Hyper Roll, Space Jackpot in that order. If that list is reordered the key lands on ANOTHER game, and any HouseEdge:* key on a non-house-edge entry seeds that type as a broken house-edge type that never opens a round — re-check the index against the committed config before deploying. (2) IT IS CREATE-ONLY: game types are seeded once, matched by name, so the value is read only when the Hyper Roll row is first created (its first deploy). HouseEdgeReconciler deliberately never touches MaximumStake, so editing this key after launch does NOTHING; changing a live max stake is a guarded UPDATE of GameParameters.MaximumStake plus deleting the ActiveParameters:v2 Redis key. GeneralSettings:Games:HouseEdgeTimeUntilGameStarts is the countdown in seconds from a Hyper Roll round's bet to the race (decision 28, amended by decision 35: every round is solo, so it is 0 and the round starts immediately); a global setting — missing falls back to TimeUntilGameStarts, and 0 means start immediately. Both keys are plain config, not secrets: no Terraform binding needed. GeneralSettings:Games:HouseEdgeEnabled (decision 33, 2026-09-16; default true when missing) is a maintenance switch: disabling it refuses NEW Hyper Roll bets with the maintenance message and shows a MAINTENANCE badge on the lobby card, while rounds already in play still settle; flipping it is a redeploy of API + Consumers. Every bet is also refused and refunded with that same message when the treasury cannot cover the round's worst case, so keep the treasury funded.
_comment_streamers: STREAMER WALLETS (#201): wallets listed under GeneralSettings:Operator:Streamers:Wallets play the house-edge games (Hyper Roll, House duel) with a fixed PLAY-MONEY balance instead of paying real stakes. The values are PUBLIC wallet addresses, so they live in appConfig (not secrets). Config is INSERT-ONLY: the StreamerWallets table is the source of truth, so removing a wallet here does nothing (switch its row's Active off in the DB). Adding a wallet or a top-up here needs a FULL deploy (`deploy --env <env>`): a component deploy never applies appConfig. TopUps ids must be UNIQUE and NEVER REUSED (an id is applied once; reusing one silently skips the credit). Streamer bets are excluded from leaderboards, stats money and partner turnover. MOCK_ values here are placeholders: replace them, or drop the Wallets/TopUps keys when no streamer is configured.
_comment_staff: STAFF BADGES (#205): GeneralSettings:Admins:N / GeneralSettings:Moderators:N are PUBLIC wallet addresses (appConfig, never secrets) whose chat messages, DMs and profile show an ADM / MOD badge. One key per wallet, numbered from 0 (GeneralSettings:Admins:0, :1, ...); no key = an empty list. A wallet in both lists shows as ADM. The badge is display-only - it grants no admin powers (those stay on the AdminToken).
_comment_leaderboard_reset: Leaderboards:WeeklyResetAnchorUtc anchors the WEEKLY boards' reset grid: they rank the slot {anchor + k*7d} containing now. 2026-09-30T15:00:00Z is Wednesday 15:00 UTC = 12:00 BRT (UTC-3, no DST in Brazil since 2019). Only the WEEKDAY and TIME-OF-DAY matter, not the date. Editing it re-cuts every live week at once. Omit or null it to fall back to a rolling 7-day window. It is appConfig, NOT a secret: no Terraform binding needed.
_comment_analytics: GA4: ONE measurement id serves BOTH properties — the app reads VUE_APP_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and the landing page reads PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, so set them to the SAME G-XXXXXXXXXX. Both live in frontBuild because the deploy tool writes that same block into BOTH repo builds and each toolchain only exposes its own prefix (Vue CLI: VUE_APP_*, Astro/Vite: PUBLIC_*). ⚠️ OMITTING PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID SHIPPED THE LANDING PAGE WITH NO ANALYTICS AT ALL, silently, for as long as it took a paid campaign to notice (Bitmedia, Aug 2026): Layout.astro wraps the whole tag in `{gaId && ...}`, so an unresolved id renders nothing, no error, no empty property — www. just had no data while app. reported normally. The LP now FALLS BACK to VUE_APP_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID (frontmatter is server-side, where Vite exposes unprefixed vars too), so a block carrying only the Vue name still works — but set BOTH anyway; the fallback is a safety net, not the contract. ⚠️ The shared _ga cookie does NOT by itself keep the LP -> app hop one session: Consent Mode defaults analytics_storage to denied, so no cookie exists until the visitor accepts. What carries the campaign is Layout.astro forwarding the utm_* params onto every GAME_URL link (see marketing/utm-conventions.md). EMPTY = analytics never loads: no script, no cookie, no consent banner — keep them empty in secrets.development.json so dev never reports into the production property. The id is public in the page source, so it is config rather than a credential, but still never commit a real one.
_comment_orbit_flag: ORBIT FRONTEND GATE (#146): VUE_APP_ORBIT_ENABLED in frontBuild decides whether the SPA SHOWS Orbit; the three Orbit secrets above decide whether the BACKEND engine is configured. They are independent — the engine keeps running on a flag-off build, which is safe only while no player is enrolled and no game type has AllowOrbit=true (verify that once against production before deploying with the flag off). FAIL-CLOSED: only the exact string 'true' enables it, so omitting the key ships Orbit hidden. production: 'false' (not production-deliverable yet); development: 'true'.
_comment_token_mint: TOKEN LAUNCH (#160): ONE value — the SPL MINT ADDRESS of the launched pump.fun token — serves BOTH builds. The app reads VUE_APP_TOKEN_MINT and the landing page reads PUBLIC_TOKEN_MINT, so set them to the SAME address; both live in frontBuild because the deploy tool writes that block into both repo builds and each toolchain only exposes its own prefix. EMPTY = the PRE-LAUNCH state on both sites: the LP keeps its 'No token. Yet.' panel with the anti-scam warning, and the app renders no token card and no header token button. FAIL-CLOSED — anything that is not a plausible base58 mint is treated as empty, so a Buy button can never point at nothing. WARNING: THIS IS NOT VUE_APP_GAME_TOKEN_ADDRESS. That is the SETTLEMENT mint the games actually pay out in; the two are independent, and conflating them means changing one silently changes the other. Rounds settle in USDC and this token is information only. WARNING: both sites are STATIC builds, so filling this in is a REBUILD + REDEPLOY OF TWO SITES, not a runtime toggle — launch day must deploy both or they disagree. The mint is public information rather than a credential, but keep it empty here and in development; the real value belongs in secrets.production.json.
_comment_treasury_wallet: TOKEN LAUNCH (#160): the address holding the game treasury. ONE value, BOTH builds — the landing page reads PUBLIC_TREASURY_WALLET and the app reads VUE_APP_TREASURY_WALLET, so set them to the SAME address. Two sites publishing two different treasuries is worse than neither publishing one. Rendered on both as a copyable bar with a Solscan link: on the LP inside its treasury block, in the app inside the /how-to-play token section (the app stopped pointing at the landing page for this on 2026-08-12 — the manual is the surface that states the real figures). EMPTY = that address bar is simply not rendered on either site; the rest of the treasury block (the supply chart and the legend) still shows, because the split is content and lives in each repo's constants file, not here. FAIL-CLOSED — anything that is not a plausible base58 address is treated as empty, so neither site can ever publish a truncated or half-typed wallet. Independent of the mint: a build may legitimately have a live mint and no wallet configured. This is a PUBLIC address, never a private key: the treasury's key material must never appear in this file or any other. Like the mint, it is baked into static builds, so filling it in is a rebuild + redeploy of BOTH sites.
_comment_new_game_delay: ROUND ROLLOVER HOLD (#180): VUE_APP_NEW_GAME_DELAY is how long, in ms, the ended round's result stays on screen before the app switches to the next round. ⚠️ THIS KEY HAD NEVER BEEN IN THIS BLOCK, under this name or the older VUE_APP_NEW_SESSION_DELAY — and monkify-front tracks only .env.example (.env.production/.env.local are git-ignored), so a deploy clone had no value from anywhere and production silently ran the hardcoded 30000 for the lifetime of the knob. At 30000 the player landed ~5s INTO the next race, because the backend opens the successor immediately, gives it a 15s betting window and then a 10s countdown; on a table that fills itself they could never bet on a rolling round at all. 9000 leaves ~6s of betting plus the whole countdown. The code default in monkify-front/src/constants/gameTiming.ts is ALSO 9000, so a deployment that never copies this key across is still correct — this entry exists to make the knob reachable, not to carry the value. ⚠️ It is also the CAP: at 9s the app rolls over whether or not the payout finished, which is deliberate (waiting for it is what used to strand a tab on a dead view). Practice mode reads the same constant, so changing this retunes /game/practice with it. Baked into a STATIC build — changing it is a rebuild + redeploy, not a runtime toggle.
